paper.title_en: Dimensional dependence of critical phenomena in black hole interiors
paper.abstract_en: Black hole interiors exhibit a critical transition in which a perturbed inner horizon either survives or collapses into a spacelike singularity, but whether the exponent governing this transition depends on spacetime dimension has remained an open question. In this paper, we numerically investigate the interior dynamics of $D$ dimensional Reissner-Nordström (RN) black holes perturbed by a real scalar field. Strong perturbations destroy the null inner horizon and produce a spacelike singularity, whereas weaker perturbations preserve it with an areal radius that decreases as the perturbation amplitude increases. As the initial scalar field amplitude $p$ approaches its critical value $p^{*}$, the inner horizon radius decreases continuously to zero. Near criticality, this radius obeys the power law $r_{s}\propto|p-p^{*}|^γ$. In four dimensions, different initial scalar field profiles and initial RN black hole charges yield nearly identical critical exponents, $γ\simeq1/2$, supporting the universality of the scaling law. Within the investigated range $4\leq D\leq9$, the critical exponent decreases systematically with increasing spacetime dimension. The numerical results suggest the scaling relation $r_s\propto|p-p^{*}|^{1/(D-2)}$. This result establishes a new dimension-dependent universality class for interior black hole critical phenomena, distinct from the standard Choptuik collapse scaling.
